questions.question: What is Brownian motion?
options: The continuous movement of water through plant roots
The random motion of particles suspended in a medium
The chemical reaction between an acid and an alkali
The process of a solid changing state directly into a gas

questions.question: How does increasing the temperature of a gas or solution affect its particles?
options: The particles move more quickly.
The particles stop moving entirely.
The particles move more slowly.
The particles decrease in number.

questions.question: Why is a suspension different from a true solution?
options: Solid particles in a suspension can be seen and will settle over time.
Suspensions can never contain liquid particles.
Suspensions are completely clear and transparent.
Particles in a suspension are permanently destroyed.

questions.question: What must be overcome between solute particles in order for a substance to dissolve?
options: Forces of gravity acting on the beaker
Atmospheric pressure around the container
Forces of attraction between solute particles
Chemical bonds within the liquid medium

questions.question: Why can mixing two liquids sometimes result in a total volume that is less than expected?
options: Particles of one substance fit into spaces between particles of the other.
Some of the liquid particles are completely destroyed during mixing.
The liquids react to form a heavy solid at the bottom.
The mass of the liquids vanishes into the air.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes dissolving and melting?
options: Both are chemical reactions that form new products.
Neither requires energy changes to occur.
Dissolving is a chemical change, while melting is a physical change.
Dissolving is not the same as melting, but both are physical processes.

questions.question: When is a solution formed?
options: When an insoluble solid settles at the bottom of a container
When a soluble solid dissolves in an appropriate solvent
When two immiscible liquids separate into two layers
When a gas turns into a solid without becoming a liquid

questions.question: If 10 g of salt is completely dissolved in 100 g of water, what is the total mass of the resulting solution?
Which piece of equipment and unit are standard for measuring liquid volume in the laboratory?
options: Balance, measured in grams (g)
Thermometer, measured in degrees Celsius (°C)
Measuring cylinder, measured in cm³
Ruler, measured in mm

questions.question: How can laboratory equipment be visually communicated in scientific reports?
options: 2D drawings/images
3D painted sculptures
Written paragraphs only, with no diagrams
Photographs of random objects

questions.question: What defines a pure material in chemistry?
options: It contains a mixture of three or more elements.
It is made of only one type of substance.
It is always transparent and liquid.
It dissolves instantly in any liquid.

questions.question: What is true about the melting and boiling points of a pure material?
options: They change continuously depending on the time of day.
They cannot be measured in a laboratory.
They are fixed and constant.
They vary widely across a broad range of temperatures.

questions.question: How do impurities affect the melting and boiling points of a material?
options: They keep the melting and boiling points completely unchanged.
They change the melting and boiling point of the material.
They prevent the substance from ever boiling or melting.
They force the boiling point to equal room temperature.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a mixture?
options: It contains only one element chemically bonded together.
It contains two or more types of substances which can be easily separated.
It cannot be separated by physical methods like filtration.
It has a single, fixed chemical composition.

questions.question: Unlike pure substances, how do mixtures melt or boil?
options: At a single precise temperature point
Over a range of temperatures
Without absorbing or releasing heat
Only when placed under vacuum

questions.question: At a given temperature, what limit exists when dissolving a solute in a solvent?
options: Infinite amounts of solute can keep dissolving forever.
There is a limit to how much solute can dissolve in a solvent.
The solvent will immediately turn into a gas.
The solute will turn into a completely new element.

questions.question: What can happen to a dissolved solute as a warm solution cools down?
options: The solute may become insoluble and form solid particles.
The mass of the solute multiplies.
The solvent turns into solid metal.
The solute permanently evaporates.

questions.question: Which of the following factors can affect the solubility of a substance?
options: The shape of the lab bench
The choice or temperature of the solvent
The color of the measuring cylinder
The time of day the experiment is done

questions.question: In a scientific investigation, what is the independent variable?
options: The variable that is kept constant to make the test fair
The variable that is changed in the investigation
The final conclusion written at the end
The measurement tool used to collect data

questions.question: What are variables called when they are kept the same each time in an experiment?
options: Dependent variables
Independent variables
Control variables
Random variables
